2027-01-15.title: Friday after the First Sunday after Denho · Commemoration of Mary, Mother of God, for the Seeds
readings: God supplies seed to the sower
2027-01-15.alt: Season of Denho. Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of Muvattupuzha (2003).
2027-01-15.verse: He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
theo: The Syriac Churches keep in January a commemoration of the Mother of God for the seeds: at the season of sowing, farmers brought their seed to church to be blessed, entrusting the year's harvest to the prayers of Mary. Paul's words fit perfectly: “the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.” And: “He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed.” Generosity is sowing; God gives the growth.

In the Gospel Mary receives the shepherds' story and “treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” Mary is the good soil where the Word is sown and bears fruit. Today we pray for farmers and for all who work the land, for a good harvest and fair prices, and for the Eparchy of Muvattupuzha on its anniversary. Let our hearts, like Mary's, receive the seed of God's word, and let our hands sow generously.
outline: Ask: what are you sowing in your life this year?
live: Pray today for farmers, and buy something directly from a local farmer this week.
Give cheerfully to one person in need this week.
2027-01-15.prayer: God who gives seed to the sower and bread for food, through the prayers of the Mother of God bless the seed of our farmers and the work of our hands. Make our hearts good soil for your word, as Mary's was, and make us cheerful givers. Amen.
altar: Bread and wine come from seed sown in the earth. At the Qurbono, the fruit of the earth and work of human hands becomes the Body and Blood of Christ.

quick: Those who sow bountifully reap bountifully.
God supplies the seed and gives the growth.
Mary is the good soil where the Word bears fruit.
2027-01-15.action: Give cheerfully to one person in need this week.
2027-01-15.question: Is my heart good soil for God's word?

family.explain: St Paul says: if you plant many seeds, you will get a big harvest. God loves people who give with a happy heart.
family.intention: We pray for farmers who grow our food.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share happily with someone this week?”

illus: In some Malankara parishes farmers still bring a small bag of paddy seed to church in January to be blessed before sowing. One elderly farmer in Kunnamkulam said: I have done this for fifty years. The rain is not in my hands, but the seed is in God's hands and Mother Mary's prayers.

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, through the prayers of the Mother of God, bless our sowing and make us cheerful givers. Amen.
share: The one who sows bountifully will reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). What am I sowing?
God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:7). Do I give cheerfully?
Mary treasured all these words (Luke 2:19). Do I treasure God's word?
pm.resp: Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For a good monsoon and a good harvest.
For the hungry, that they may share in the harvest.
For our group, that we may be good soil for God's word.
pm.close: Father, you give seed to the sower and bread for food. Bless our labour and make us generous, through the prayers of Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today our tradition remembers the Mother of God for the seeds. At sowing time farmers brought their seed to be blessed and entrusted the harvest to Mary's prayers.

Paul says: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. God loves a cheerful giver (2 Corinthians 9:6–7). Generosity is like sowing.
And God is the true giver: he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed (2 Corinthians 9:10). All growth is grace.

In the Gospel Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She is the good soil where the Word was sown. Let us pray for our farmers and for Muvattupuzha eparchy, and let our hearts receive the Word as Mary did. Amen.
kids: Children, a tiny seed can become a big plant! Mary kept God's words in her heart like seeds. Let us keep Jesus' words in our hearts too.

intro: Sowing generously, God's gift of growth, Mary the good soil.

q: Some give freely, yet grow all the richer; others withhold what is due, and only suffer want.
The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
points.apply: Give cheerfully to someone in need this week.

q: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease.”
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
points.apply: Pray for farmers and a good harvest.

q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Ponder one Gospel verse each day.

concl: God gives the seed; we sow generously.
Mary shows how the Word bears fruit.
2027-01-15.resolve: Support a farmer or share food with the hungry this week.
